purpose: A successor to the C-2 head c2-plan-stage-schema.v9.json, scoped to exactly two findings and to nothing else. FINDING 1: executionPlanCommitment is required in three closed records and has no stated semantics anywhere in this corpus; artifacts/execution-plan-commitment.investigation.v1.json ruled the question UNDETERMINED, it is a freeze section 7.1 parked row, and freeze section 6 law 19 places the ruling in this artifact and nowhere else. This candidate rules it an ALIAS of planIntentCommitment, derives that ruling from the closed ExecutionPlan envelope rather than from a list of records, acknowledges the resulting duplication normatively, and publishes the separating vector the freeze records as stated and unexercised -- executed here rather than asserted. FINDING 2: the head's documentSkeleton.sha256 and its 29 root-subtree digests depend on a frame format that exists only inside check-c2-v9.py, while the head describes it only as 'length-framed, type-tagged', which many mutually incompatible encodings satisfy. The head's totality argument was therefore carried by digests no contract reader could recompute, which is the property freeze section 7.1 names. This candidate lifts that frame format into the contract as normative text and demonstrates sufficiency by reproducing the head's published digests with two encoders written from the new text alone. It is a DERIVATION in the shape the head itself uses: the effective contract is the verified predecessor with the listed operations applied and nothing else. It binds nothing.

value.ruling: ALIAS. executionPlanCommitment is not a second commitment. It is a second WIRE POSITION carrying the value this contract already defines at planIntent.canonicalCommitment: the planIntentCommitment of the ExecutionPlan in question. C-2 mints no ExecutionPlan commitment namespace and no ExecutionPlan domain separator, because the ExecutionPlan already has a commitment over itself, and it is planId.
value.authority: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 19 reserves an identity namespace and its domain separator to the surface that owns the identity, in that surface's own binding artifact. C-2 owns ExecutionPlan. This block is that surface speaking. artifacts/execution-plan-commitment.investigation.v1.json ruled the question UNDETERMINED, recorded that it can be settled only here, and measured that this contract contained the string zero times; this block is the response to that measurement.
value.requiredValue: Wherever a record carries a field named executionPlanCommitment for an ExecutionPlan, its value MUST be byte-identical to that ExecutionPlan's planIntentCommitment, computed by planIntent.canonicalCommitment and by nothing else. There is no second recipe, no second preimage and no second domain separator.

theDerivation.why: The ruling is derived from a structural property of the closed ExecutionPlan envelope, not from a list of the records that happen to carry the field today. A property quantified over the closed field set stays true for records this contract has never seen; a list does not.
theDerivation.step1ClosedEnvelope: executionPlan.closedTopLevel is true and executionPlan.requiredFields is the closed six-list [snapshotId, planId, projectId, planIntentCommitment, planIdentityInputs, stages]; attemptAndExecutionJoin.executionPlanRequired states the same six. An ExecutionPlan therefore cannot carry a member named executionPlanCommitment at all -- the envelope is closed and the name is not in it. That is a positive statement of this contract, not silence about the field.
theDerivation.step2PlanIdIsAlreadyTheCommitment: Every one of the six closed fields is bound, by this contract's own attemptAndExecutionJoin.equalityRule together with the joined PLAN-ID-V1 preimage, to a field of that preimage: snapshotId to preimage tag 1; projectId to descriptor.scope.projectId and scope is tag 6; planIntentCommitment to tag 13; planIdentityInputs to the thirteen preimage fields themselves; stages to descriptor.workflow.stages and workflow is tag 11; and planId to the digest of that preimage, which PLAN-ID-V1 excludes from its own input so the definition is not recursive. Two ExecutionPlans carrying the same planId are therefore equal at every field a closed ExecutionPlan has.
theDerivation.step3Conclusion: planId IS a commitment over the ExecutionPlan. A distinct executionPlanCommitment would be a second digest over the same closed envelope, computed from the same inputs under a different framing -- a redundant second identity for one object, in a corpus whose section 8 failure list already names inventing a second authority for one thing. Law 19 permits C-2 to mint an ExecutionPlan identity; it does not oblige C-2 to mint a second one, and there is no information the second could carry that the first does not.
theDerivation.step4WhatFollowsForConsumers: Any record that identifies an executed plan already identifies it by planId, because planId is the ExecutionPlan's identity in the surface that owns ExecutionPlan and PLAN-ID-V1 is this corpus's only ExecutionPlan identity. A record carrying executionPlanCommitment but NOT planId would be identifying an execution by a commitment this contract does not define, and is INVALID under this ruling until C-2 defines one.
theDerivation.confirmingMeasurement: Measured on the corpus as it stands, and offered as a confirmation of the derived property rather than as its basis: the three records that require the field each carry planId in the same record, adjacent to both commitment positions -- ActivationManifestV1 fieldOrder [schemaVersion, projectId, planId, planIntentCommitment, executionPlanCommitment, ...], EvaluationAuthoritySealV1 the same, and TerminalRunV1 at tags 0xb3 planId, 0xb4 planIntentCommitment, 0xb5 executionPlanCommitment. The separating input is therefore already separated inside those very records, by planId. Nothing a new commitment could add is missing.

whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.shapeConsidered: A distinct recipe with its own domain separator, minted here under law 19, plus a vector in which two ExecutionPlans share a planIntentCommitment and differ.
whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.itIsLawful: It is lawful. Law 19 permits C-2 to mint it and no sentence in the corpus forbids it. It is rejected on the merits, not on authority.
whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.reason1Redundancy: It would give one closed object two commitments derived from the same inputs. theDerivation step 2 shows planId already separates exactly the ExecutionPlans a second commitment would separate.
whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.reason2ItWouldFalsifyEveryExistingSite: A distinct domain separator makes the two values differ ALWAYS, not merely sometimes. The investigation measured 139 sites over 16 files carrying this field, 132 of them alongside a planIntentCommitment, with 132 equal and 0 differing. Minting a distinct recipe declares all 139 sites wrong at once, in reviewed bytes that section 7.2 forbids editing in place. A ruling that invalidates every existing instance of the thing it rules on should be reached only when the evidence forces it, and here the evidence points the other way: the investigation reconstructed BOTH distinct values and found each to be SHA-256 over a domain-tagged PlanIntent at 2463 bytes. Nothing in this corpus has ever computed a commitment over an ExecutionPlan.
whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.reason3TheTagsDoNotImplyIt: Distinct wire tags prove two framed POSITIONS in one record. Under the componentFrame TLV grammar each field is independently framed, so two tags carrying one value is exactly as well-formed as two tags carrying two. Inferring difference from tag distinctness is the inference the freeze row explicitly withdraws, and this ruling does not make it.
whyNotTheOtherLawfulShape.reason4NameIsNotNature: This contract's own intentBindingFixtures already contain a fixture named reject-execution-plan-commitment-substitution whose mutation sets the ExecutionPlan's planIntentCommitment. In this corpus the phrase 'execution plan commitment' has already been used to mean 'the commitment field carried ON the execution plan'. That is a reading of the NAME which the alias ruling makes coherent and a distinct recipe would make ambiguous.

duplicationAcknowledged.statement: This ruling leaves a REDUNDANT REQUIRED FIELD in three closed records. The redundancy is real, it is a defect, and stating it is part of the ruling rather than an aside. A ruling that made the corpus tidy by pretending the second position carries information would be the failure this lineage keeps repairing.
duplicationAcknowledged.whatItCosts: Each record frames one value twice at two distinct tags. A verifier that treats the two positions as independent inputs believes it has checked two things when it has checked one. That is a false assurance, and it is the concrete harm of the duplication.
duplicationAcknowledged.whatIsRequiredOfAConsumer: The two positions MUST carry one value. A record in which they differ is INVALID and MUST be REJECTED. Under this ruling equality is the field's DEFINITION, not an incidental property of the fixtures -- which is precisely the status it did not have before, when three checkers asserted it and no generation produced it.
duplicationAcknowledged.migrationDirection: A future major of any record carrying both SHOULD carry planId and planIntentCommitment and drop executionPlanCommitment. C-2 does not schedule that and cannot: the tag assignments live in EVALUATION-PROOF and EVIDENCE bytes, and section 7.2 forbids editing reviewed bytes. This is a direction recorded for whoever writes those successors, not an instruction this artifact can execute.
duplicationAcknowledged.whatThisRulingDoesNotDo: It does not edit, re-pin, re-verdict or re-seal any record that declares the tags, and it does not close the freeze section 7.1 parked row. It binds nothing until applied by a coordinator.

comparisonDiscipline.rule: Two commitments are compared by BYTE EQUALITY performed after an INDEPENDENT TYPE ASSERTION on each side. Neither side may be compared by host-language equality, under which 1, 1.0 and true are one value, and under which a set membership or subset test silently coerces.
comparisonDiscipline.why: freeze section 6 law 18. This class defeated this lineage at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, each time inside the repair's own self-certification. The vectors below are stated so that they cannot be passed by a comparison that coerces.
comparisonDiscipline.admission: The value is wire type sha256Id: a JSON STRING matching ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$. Admission is by exact JSON type and canonical spelling. Every other production of the JSON data model, and every non-canonical spelling of the same digest, is REJECTED rather than coerced. The coverage of that statement is the JSON data model itself, not a list of types this author happened to think of.

value.why: freeze section 7.1 states the property that a rule which exists only inside a checker's Python is not a binding artifact. The head publishes documentSkeleton.sha256 and 29 root-subtree digests, and describes the encoding that produces them only as 'length-framed, type-tagged'. Many mutually incompatible encodings satisfy that phrase; four of them are exhibited in the vectors below together with the byte at which they diverge. The head's totality argument -- that an added, removed, renamed, reparented or retyped node anywhere is a named finding -- is therefore carried by digests no contract reader could recompute. This block is the encoding stated normatively, so that an independent implementer reproduces those digests from the contract alone.
value.name: opensip-jx-canon-v1
value.authority: Minted by C-2 under freeze section 6 law 19: this is C-2's own document-identity encoding, in C-2's own binding artifact. It extends no other surface's closed vocabulary, so law 19's authority requirement is not engaged. It states what the pinned instrument already computes; it does not change it.
value.relationToTheChecker: check-c2-v9.py is PINNED and several checkers hash-verify it at runtime (section 7.6), so it is not edited and this candidate does not edit it. The direction of this block is contract-states-what-code-does, never code-changed-to-match-contract.
value.produces: a CHARACTER STRING -- a sequence of Unicode scalar values -- and not a byte string. Bytes appear only at the digest boundary, which is stated separately below. Conflating the two is the first way an implementer reproduces the wrong digest.
value.dataModel: The seven productions of the JSON data model: null, boolean, integer, number, string, array, object. A JSON number written with no fractional part and no exponent is an INTEGER; any other number is a NUMBER. Booleans are classified BEFORE integers. A value outside these seven is refused by name rather than guessed at.
value.frame: FRAME(tag, payload) = tag || DECIMAL(N) || ':' || payload, where N is the number of UNICODE CODE POINTS in payload.

frameParts.tag: exactly one character, taken from typeTags
frameParts.length: N in base ten as ASCII digits U+0030 to U+0039, shortest form: no leading zero unless N is zero, in which case the single character '0'. No sign, no padding, no digit separators.
frameParts.lengthIsCountedInCodePoints: N counts UNICODE CODE POINTS of the payload string. It is NOT the UTF-8 byte length, NOT the UTF-16 code-unit length and NOT a count of grapheme clusters. This is the single most under-determined point in the phrase 'length-framed', and it is the reason this block exists: the head document is pure ASCII, so its own digests cannot distinguish the readings. Vector FF-1 does.
frameParts.payload: the production body below, emitted verbatim -- no escaping, no quoting, no normalisation, no whitespace

productions.null: FRAME('z', '') -- the empty payload, so the token is z0:
productions.boolean: FRAME('b', '1') for true and FRAME('b', '0') for false
productions.integer: FRAME('i', shortest base-ten form: a single leading '-' for negative values, no leading '+', and no leading zeros except the single character '0' for zero itself)
productions.number: FRAME('n', the shortest decimal string that round-trips to the same IEEE-754 binary64 value)
productions.string: FRAME('s', the character sequence itself, verbatim and unescaped)
productions.array: FRAME('a', the concatenation of the tokens of the elements in ascending index order)
productions.object: FRAME('o', the concatenation of key-token followed by value-token over the members, in the order objectOrdering states)

objectOrdering.rule: Members are ordered by ascending (KEY TOKEN, VALUE TOKEN), compared as sequences of Unicode code points. The ordering key is the CANONICAL TOKEN of the key, not the raw key.
objectOrdering.theTrap: Those two orders are NOT the same, because the token places the length before the payload. Keys 'b' and 'ab' produce tokens s1:b and s2:ab, so 'b' precedes 'ab' under this rule while raw-key order puts 'ab' first. An implementer who sorts by raw key -- the order opensip-canonical-json-v1 uses for a different purpose -- produces a different token for the same object. Vector FF-2 is exactly that case.
objectOrdering.totality: The value token breaks ties. After duplicate-key rejection there are no ties, and the tie-break is stated so the order is total rather than merely usually-total.

value.digestBoundary: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 encoding of the token, with no byte-order mark, no trailing newline and no outer envelope in the digest input. Rendered as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

documentSkeleton.walk: Every NODE of the document, container nodes included, in pre-order depth-first order: a node is emitted before its children; object members are visited in the order the JSON text presents them, duplicate keys having been rejected by the parser; array elements are visited in ascending index order.
documentSkeleton.path: The path of a node is the ARRAY of steps from the document root to it. An object member contributes its key as a STRING step; an array element contributes its zero-based index as an INTEGER step. The root's path is the empty array.
documentSkeleton.row: [ the token of the path array , the JSON type name of the node ] -- a two-element array of two strings
documentSkeleton.skeleton: the array of rows, in walk order
documentSkeleton.sha256: the digest, as digestBoundary defines it, of the token of the skeleton array
documentSkeleton.whyThePathIsCanonicalisedAndNotRendered: IR-C2V8-01. A rendering of the path is not injective: a '/'-join with no escaping maps ['a','b'] and ['a/b'] to one text, and maps the array index 0 and the object key '0' to one text. Canonicalising the steps ARRAY is injective by construction, because the encoding is length-framed and invertible. Vectors FF-3 and FF-5 are the two collisions the rendering admits.
documentSkeleton.subtreeDigest: For each member of the root object, the same computation applied to that member's VALUE, with paths taken relative to that value, so the subtree root's path is the empty array. Its purpose is localisation: a change reported only against a whole-document digest names no position.
documentSkeleton.fixpoint: The skeleton binds PATH and JSON TYPE only, never a value. Publishing these digests inside the document they describe therefore cannot change what they describe, provided the publishing keys are present with values of unchanged JSON type.

exercisedByTheSkeletonDigest.measurement: A skeleton row is [string, string] and a path array holds strings and integers. The skeleton digest therefore exercises exactly three productions -- string, integer and array -- and does NOT exercise null, boolean, number or object.
exercisedByTheSkeletonDigest.whyTheOtherFourAreSpecifiedAnyway: Because opensip-jx-canon-v1 is TOTAL and is used for value comparison as well as for the skeleton, and because an encoding specified only where it is currently exercised is exactly the coverage-claim-over-an-unobserved-region that this contract's hostileScalarLeafTotality section exists to refuse. Stating the split is the point; a specification silently covering only what today's document happens to contain is how this corpus has repeatedly shipped a totality it could not observe.
exercisedByTheSkeletonDigest.witnessed: Vectors FF-2, FF-6 and FF-7 exercise the four otherwise-unexercised productions directly, so the specification is witnessed even where the head's own digest does not reach it.

theTwoEncodingsAreNotInterchangeable.statement: opensip-jx-canon-v1 is NOT opensip-canonical-json-v1, and neither may be substituted for the other.
theTwoEncodingsAreNotInterchangeable.differences: opensip-canonical-json-v1 (planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding) emits JSON text, sorts object keys by ascending Unicode scalar value of the KEY, applies NFC normalisation, escapes strings, and FORBIDS floating-point values. opensip-jx-canon-v1 emits a framed token, sorts by the canonical TOKEN of the key, applies no normalisation and no escaping, and is TOTAL over floating-point values because it must be able to name one in order to refuse it elsewhere.
theTwoEncodingsAreNotInterchangeable.consequence: A commitment computed with the wrong one of these is a different digest. They serve different purposes: one commits to a PlanIntent on the wire, the other identifies the shape of a contract document.

theCommitmentQuestion.finding: executionPlanCommitment is required in three closed records, is typed 'Raw commitment' -- a type used 18 times and defined nowhere -- and has no stated semantics anywhere in this corpus.
theCommitmentQuestion.priorState: artifacts/execution-plan-commitment.investigation.v1.json (0b8bb3dec4a08b8559aae751a6c0ebc3f6d59a32f74e5a4770ccdb6ff1b9a2fa, measurement-only) ruled it UNDETERMINED and it became a freeze section 7.1 parked row.
theCommitmentQuestion.where: the effective contract at planIntent.attemptAndExecutionJoin.executionPlanCommitment, added by operation 2
theCommitmentQuestion.shortRationale: The ExecutionPlan envelope is CLOSED and does not contain the name, so an ExecutionPlan cannot carry the field. Every field it does carry is bound by this contract's own equalityRule to a field of the PLAN-ID-V1 preimage, so planId is ALREADY a commitment over the whole ExecutionPlan.
